clues.title: Plate: License plates
text: A short license plate with a double blue strip on the front and a long plate with a double blue strip on the back is unique to Italy. Similar long plates with a double blue strip can be found in Albania and France, but the front plates won’t be short.

clues.title: Language: Italian Helpful Words
text: Here are a few words in Italian that can either help you identify the language quickly, be helpful in region guessing, or just help learn the general feel of the language:
**senso unico** - one way
**di** - of (helps distinguish from other romance)
**castello** - castle
**prezzi** - prices
**piazza** - plaza
**autostrada** - highway
**vietato** - prohibited
**polizia** - police
**sconto** - discount

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Street sign: Word for street in Italian
text: Italy typical uses the word "via" on their street signs. Note that "strada" also means street but is the same word in Romanian and used more commonly there.
Here are some similar words:
**strada** - street (used more commonly in rural roads)
**tangenziale** - ring road
**viale** - avenue
**circonvallezione** - ring road

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Language: Italian General Tips
text: In Italian most words end in a vowel. Example exceptions include non, il, per, con, del.
Double consonants (tt, zz, cc, ss, bb, pp, ll, gg, etc.) are frequent.
Word endings: -zione, -tà, -aggio, -mento (careful spanish and portuguese use this too)
Letter sequences: gli, gn, sci.
Features of the language include: ì and à

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: Contrary to most European licence plates, Italian plates have blue strips on either side of the plate.
Furthermore, the front plate is distinctly shorter than most European plates, which in combination with the two strips, makes it unique.
Albanian licence plates also have two blue strips, and French licence plates have a smaller strip on the right.
However, neither Albanian nor French front plates are short.

clues.title: Language: Italian
text: Italian is a Romance language and the most spoken language in Italy. Italian does not use any real special letters, only accents on top of vowels: (**À, È, É, Ì, Ò, Ó** and **Ù**).
The Italian word for street is **via**.
Italian is perhaps most often confused with Spanish. Some characteristics of Italian that can help with this distinction are:
Extensive use of double consonants
Extensive use of the letter i
Almost all words ending in a vowel

Take the text in the picture below as an example. In Italian, this text has 5 uses of double vowels, 28 uses of the letter i and 29 words ending in a vowel. The same numbers for the Spanish version are 0, 6 and 6 respectively.
